title: Who owned the Onyx and why musicians came: Carl Kress and the Casa Loma players
summary: Joe Helbock owned the club, guitarist Carl Kress drew studio men, and the Casa Loma band came nightly; Jones and trombonist Pee Wee Hunt did spontaneous jive numbers.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, so that was Joe Helvuth (PHONETIC), wasn't it. Well, did he own that club or did --
I think he owned it and I think Carl Kress, if you remember, had something to do with it.
I don't know how much. Maybe he put in some money there, too. Because Carl Kress was a great guitar player, you know.
And he'd be there practically all the time, and he was a studio man, so all the rest of the guys would come over. I imagine that helped to draw them, you know.
Over there, with Carl being one of them, you know.

So we got to know all the guys through that. The Casa Loma Band and all of them. They'd come there every night. They'd come into the Onyx, and sometimes me and Pee Wee Hunt, the trombone player, would do a little number together, you know, a little jive number, just spontaneously, you know.
